paragraphs: The GLC300 has been a core part of the GLC-Class range since the model's launch in 2015, spanning two generations under one badge. The earlier X253 generation (2015–2022) uses the M274 — a 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrol engine that was widely used across Mercedes models of that era. From 2022, the X254-generation GLC300 switched to the M254, a newer 2.0-litre four-cylinder unit that added mild-hybrid technology and increased torque from 258 lb-ft to 295 lb-ft. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and rebuild specifics differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every GLC300 on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrol engine fitted to the GLC300 from 2015 to 2022. No specific known issue has been independently confirmed for this application. We replace timing chain components, bearings and gaskets as standard during a rebuild.

A 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrol engine fitted from 2022, with mild-hybrid technology. As a newer unit, no specific known issues have been independently confirmed for this application. We service it to the same standard as our other four-cylinder petrol rebuilds.

compatibility.intro: Because the GLC300 spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an M274 part will work on an M254 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
